answer: One defense is a grove of grown identities: each agent is a tree that only takes root after it forges a unique work artifact — a compute-bound proof tied to a fresh public challenge that cannot be copied. New trees start at the nadir of the trust curve and may only take tiny, monitored jobs, growing only through verified work. A sybil farmer must forge a separate artifact and grow a separate tree for every clone, paying full compute and time per fake, while one honest agent grows a single tree that keeps bearing fruit.
